# ml-platform

> Multi-project ML platform monorepo: one shared substrate across tabular, deep
> learning, LLM and agent projects, multi-cloud.
> Version: 0.1.0 | License: Apache-2.0 | Author: DuqueOM

## What this is

A monorepo where several ML systems share one substrate — libraries, platform,
orchestration, gates and agentic surface — and each system is a **vertical**
under `projects/`. It is consumed by duplicating a vertical with the generator,
not by forking: see `docs/EXPORTING.md`.

Its distinguishing property is that **most of its rules are executable**. The
claims in this file are checked by `tests/test_llms_txt.py`, which compares
every count below against the filesystem — a document about a repository is the
easiest kind to leave true-sounding and wrong.

**Scope**: the platform layer. Service-level concerns — the serving loop,
probes, containers, K8s manifests, supply chain — are authoritative in the
sibling `ml-service-template` and consumed from it (ADR-003). `services/` here
is generated from it and not edited.

## Start here

- `AGENTS.md` — the operating constitution: invariants, the AUTO/CONSULT/STOP
  protocol, and the pre-commit cadence
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — the cadence in order, and why staging comes before
  regenerating
- `docs/architecture/technical-plan.md` — **intent**: phases, deliverables,
  acceptance commands
- `docs/architecture/implementation-status.md` — **what exists**, derived from
  the filesystem. When the two disagree, this one is correct
- `docs/decisions/` — 9 ADRs. Never deleted or renumbered; a wrong decision is
  superseded so the reasoning survives
- `SECURITY.md` — reporting, and which findings belong upstream instead

## Layout

- `libs/` — 5 shared libraries: `ml-core`, `data-contracts`, `feature-defs`,
  `llm-core`, `serving-core`
- `projects/` — 3 verticals: `demand-forecast` (tabular regression with
  conformal intervals), `rag-assistant` (retrieval over SEC filings),
  `store-assistant` (the multi-tier agent, migrated with history per ADR-002)
- `platform/` — terraform, kubernetes, observability, policies, local stack
- `orchestration/` — Airflow DAGs (business flow) and KFP pipelines (ML compute)
- `agentic/` — canonical rules, skills and workflows; the per-tool directories
  are generated pointers
- `scripts/` — the gates, the dataset fetchers, the derived-document generators
- `services/` — generated from ml-service-template, owned upstream, not edited
- `ops/` — append-only, hash-chained audit trail

## Agentic surface

Canonical in `agentic/`: **23 rules, 29 skills, 22 workflows**. Four tool
surfaces (`.claude/`, `.cursor/`, `.codex/`, `.devin/`) are rendered from it by
`scripts/sync_agentic_adapters.py`; `--check` enforces parity in CI. Editing a
generated pointer instead of the canonical source is the mistake it exists to
catch.

## How a claim is proven

Every row in the status document carries the layer its evidence reaches, and
the layer is derived from the command that ran — never declared:

- **L1** contract: the test suite passes (CI)
- **L2** component: the thing itself executes (CI)
- **L3** cluster: it starts and answers in kind (a machine with Docker)
- **L4** cloud: a real rollout on GKE or EKS

Nothing generated in CI can display L3 or L4. Higher-layer evidence is named as
a command and marked *not run here*. L4 is printed at zero on purpose.

## The gates

Every published quality claim maps to a command that can fail a build. The
count and the full table live in `docs/governance/quality-gates.md`, which is
where a number can be checked; this file is hand-written and a figure copied
into it drifts the moment a gate is added. The ones worth knowing:

- `scripts/check_doc_coherence.py` — C1–C9: ADR index integrity against git
  history, dangling references, gate traceability, private-name denylist,
  independent-audit freshness, copier pinning
- `scripts/check_implementation_status.py` — derives status; `--check` fails on
  a stale committed copy
- `scripts/check_thresholds.py` — 9 gated numbers, compared against git HEAD.
  They may rise and may not fall
- `scripts/check_upstream_parity.py` — every artifact ml-service-template has,
  this repository has decided about
- `tests/test_project_contract.py` — the 7 requirements every vertical meets

## Invariants that carry the most weight

- **A gate must be verified by injection.** Break what it guards, watch it
  fail, restore, and record it. A coherence filter here once matched absolute
  paths, examined zero files, and passed
- The derived documents are never hand-edited; editing a tick does not make it
  true and CI notices
- Lowering a quality-gate threshold, and deleting or renumbering an ADR, are
  STOP operations with gates behind them
- A project depends only downward: `libs/` never imports `projects/`, and
  projects never import each other
- `~=` for ML pins — `numpy 2.x` corrupts joblib artifacts
- No static cloud credentials: Workload Identity on GCP, IRSA on AWS

## Current state, honestly

Component totals move on every commit, so they are not repeated here — read
`docs/architecture/implementation-status.md`, which derives them.

One number is worth stating because it changes only once: **0 at L4**. Nothing
in this repository has ever run in a cloud. The plan's first sequencing
constraint says it will not until everything else is finished, and the day that
stops being true is a milestone, not a routine update.
